overview: The Oil Palm Area Expansion (OPAE) Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) launched by the Government of India to promote oil palm cultivation and enhance domestic edible oil availability. The scheme aims to increase oil palm area from 3.5 lakh hectares to 10 lakh hectares by 2025-26, with a focus on North-Eastern States and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. It provides financial assistance for planting material, maintenance, drip irrigation, bore-wells, vermi-compost units, machinery, and small tractors, with viability gap payment for Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) linked to industry procurement. The scheme is implemented through State Departments of Agriculture/Horticulture in coordination with processors and other stakeholders.
geographic_scope: Pan-India (20 states covering 284 districts including NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands)
objectives: Increase area of oil palm to 10 lakh hectares from 3.5 lakh ha during 2019-20 by 2025-26
Increase Crude Palm Oil production from 0.27 lakh tonnes during 2019-20 to 11.20 lakh tonnes by 2025-26 and 28 lakh tonnes by 2028-29
Increase consumer awareness to maintain consumption level of 19.00 kg/person/annum till 2025-26
Enhance edible oilseeds production and oils availability in the country by harnessing Oil Palm area expansion
Reduce import burden on edible oils
Provide Viability price of FFBs to farmers linked with assured procurement by the industry
Central government to compensate farmers through viability gap payment if price paid by industry is below viability price up to October 2037
Bring additional area of 6.5 lakh ha under Oil Palm plantation with 3.28 lakh ha in north-eastern states and 3.22 lakh ha in Rest of India from 2021-22 to 2025-26
eligibility: Farmers (including SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women, and NE states beneficiaries) in 20 states covering 284 districts identified by ICAR-IIOPR as suitable for oil palm cultivation, including NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands. State Governments will develop long-term agreements between farmers, processors and states through the Oil Palm Act or any other mechanism prevalent in the state. Processors, ICAR, KVKs, SAUs, CAUs, CDDs, and other stakeholders are involved in formulation, prioritization of activities, and identification of beneficiaries at grass root level. No area restriction is applicable for individual farmers for availing subsidy/intervention.
benefits: Financial assistance for planting material @ 85% cost of Rs. 12,000/ha for entire land during first year for plantation and Rs. 10,000/ha/year for maintenance cost of new plantations and purchasing inputs for intercropping for four years during gestation period for entire land. Installation of drip-irrigation systems as per PMSKY. 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 27,000/pump-set for diesel/electric pump-sets for SC/ST/Small & Marginal Farmers, Women and NE states beneficiaries and Rs. 22,500/pump-set for other beneficiaries. 50% cost limited to Rs. 50,000/unit for bore-well and water harvesting structures/ponds; 50% cost limited to Rs. 1.50 lakh per unit in plain area and Rs. 1.80 lakh per unit in hilly areas. For construction of vermi-compost units: 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 15,000/unit. For purchase of machinery & tools: 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 1500/- per oil palm cutter, Rs. 15,000/- per wire-mesh, Rs. 10,000/- per motorized chisel, Rs. 3000/- per unit for aluminium portable ladder, Rs. 20,000/- per unit for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states and Rs. 16,000/- per unit for other beneficiaries as per SMAM norms. 40% of the cost limited to Rs. 1.80 lakh for other beneficiary and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Small Farmers/Women/NE states for small tractor of 20HP with trolley. In case of North Eastern States, 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 250.00 lakhs is provided to the State Government for setting up a new oil palm processing mill with capacity of 5 MT per hour. 50% of the actual cost estimated by PWD/CPWD limited to 20% of the total outlay of the state under AAP for NFSM-Oil Palm for roads from oil palm field to nearest FFB collection/processing centre. Viability Gap payment: Central government compensates farmers if price paid by industry is below viability price up to October 2037.
financial_support: Financial assistance is provided as subsidy for various components: planting material (85% of Rs. 12,000/ha), maintenance (Rs. 10,000/ha/year for 4 years), drip irrigation (as per PMSKY), pump-sets (50% cost up to Rs. 27,000 for SC/ST/Women/NE and Rs. 22,500 for others), bore-wells/water harvesting (50% cost up to Rs. 50,000/unit, with higher limits in hilly areas), vermi-compost units (50% cost up to Rs. 15,000/unit), machinery & tools (50% cost up to specified limits), and small tractors (40% cost up to Rs. 1.80 lakh for others and Rs. 2.25 lakh for SC/ST/Women/NE). In NE States, 50% cost up to Rs. 250 lakhs for State Government to set up oil palm processing mills and 50% of actual cost for roads limited to 20% of state AAP outlay. Viability Gap funding: ₹1163 crore (₹1144 crore for Rest of India and ₹19.00 crore for NE states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands till 2025-26). The total estimated cost of NMEO (Oil Palm) is ₹8844 crore (GOI share ₹2196 crore, state share, and total ₹11,040 crore). Fund flow is through DBT and escrow account mechanism. For UTs and central agencies, funding is 100% GOI share. For general states: 60:40 (GOI:State); for NE states: 90:10 (GOI:State) in all components except R&D, seed gardens, nurseries, and viability gap payment (100% GOI share).
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
caveats: No permanent posts will be created by the Central or State Governments under NMEO-OP
In case of North Eastern States, 50% of the cost limited to Rs. 250.00 lakhs is provided to the State Government for setting up a new oil palm processing mill
Viability Gap payment is applicable only if price paid by industry is below viability price up to October 2037

Funding pattern is 60:40 for general states and 90:10 for NE states between Central and State Governments in all components except R&D projects, seed gardens, nurseries and viability gap payment (100% GOI share)
The assistance will be provided for water harvesting & irrigation through PRI and the details are given as Annexure-III
Release of Central and States’ share for this scheme will be through an escrow account mechanism
